structure: Part 15, the address picker and editing an address, read every non-unit-test file under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/ (party-picker.controller.js, party-picker.njk, _address-picker.njk, _cells.njk, selection.js, request-params.js, test-support.js, and view-model/index.js, pagination.js, table-rows.js, address-lines.js, error-summary.js, results-href.js) and party-edit/ (party-edit.controller.js, party-edit.njk, address-rules.js, edit-href.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js), plus the feature's parties.js and copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, and the two fit specs fit/hub-picker.fit.spec.js (907 lines, 9 describe blocks: addresses hub, the same-as shortcut, the hub without JavaScript, who is asked for a CPH number, the permanent address section, party picker per role, party picker layout, party picker save, party picker search, party picker search without JavaScript, party picker details) and fit/party-edit.fit.spec.js (5 tests). It covered the five party picker pages (place-of-origin/select, consignors/select, consignees/select, importers/select, destinations/select) and the six party edit pages (the same five plus consignment/contact/edit): their routes, caption, heading, hints, search box, results heading and count, no-matches state, table columns and cells, the radio select control, the View link into the INS address book, paging at eight a page with its fallbacks, the 'Selected address' inset restatement, the Add a new address handshake button, the handshake error and success banner, every refusal message, the edit form's nine fields with labels, hints, widths, autocomplete, required-or-optional status and length caps, its error messages, its Save changes and Cancel buttons and its return rules. Supporting files outside the slice were read only for the verbatim strings and helpers these pages use: shared/copy.en.js (addressHandshake, saveActions), shared/paging.js, shared/paths.js, shared/trail.js, shared/kit.js, common/helpers/ins-address-book-urls.js, services/address-book/index.js and features/addresses/page.js and ins-handshake.js. Welsh copy was read for key parity only. The addresses hub page itself, the same-as shortcut, the CPH and permanent-address sections and the address-return hand-off belong to part 14; where fit/hub-picker.fit.spec.js proves something about them it is claimed here, because part 14 does not read that spec, and each such claim says so in its note.

const numbersToShow = (page, totalPages) => {

claims.statement: The edit form asks nine questions in this order: name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, country, phone number and email address.
claims.quote:
export const FIELD_RULES = {
  name: { maxLength: 255, required: true },
  addressLine1: { maxLength: 255, required: true },
  addressLine2: { maxLength: 255, required: false },
  townOrCity: { maxLength: 100, required: true },
  county: { maxLength: 100, required: false },
  postcode: { maxLength: 12, required: true },
  countryCode: { required: true },
  phone: { maxLength: 20, required: true },
  email: { maxLength: 254, required: true, email: true }
}

claims.statement: The edit form's field labels read 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country', 'Phone number' and 'Email address'.
claims.quote:
fields: {
    name: 'Name or organisation name',
    addressLine1: 'Address line 1',
    addressLine2: 'Address line 2 (optional)',
    townOrCity: 'Town or city',
    county: 'County (optional)',
    postcode: 'Postcode or Zip code',
    countryCode: 'Country',
    phone: 'Phone number',
    email: 'Email address'
  },
claims.note: Address line 2 and County carry '(optional)' in the label rather than as a hint; no other field is marked optional.

claims.statement: The phone number field carries the hint 'For international numbers include the country code'.
claims.quote: phoneHint: 'For international numbers include the country code',
claims.note: It is the only hint on the form; no other field has one.

claims.statement: The country question is a plain GOV.UK select whose first option reads 'Select a country', followed by the address book's countries by name.

claims.statement: The country must be one of the address book countries the select offered; a code that is not one of them is refused.
claims.quote: requiredOneOf('countryCode', countryCodes, errors.countryCode.required),

claims.statement: A blank name is refused with 'Enter a name', and a name over the cap with 'Name must be 255 characters or fewer'.
A blank address line 1 is refused with 'Enter address line 1', and one over the cap with 'Address line 1 must be 255 characters or fewer'.
An address line 2 over the cap is refused with 'Address line 2 must be 255 characters or fewer', and it has no required message because it may be left blank.
A blank town or city is refused with 'Enter a town or city', and one over the cap with 'Town or city must be 100 characters or fewer'.
A county over the cap is refused with 'County must be 100 characters or fewer', and it has no required message because it may be left blank.
A blank postcode is refused with 'Enter a postcode', and one over the cap with 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer'.
claims.note: The label reads 'Postcode or Zip code' while the messages say only 'Postcode'.

claims.statement: No country chosen is refused with 'Enter a country'.
claims.note: The control is a select, so the message says 'Enter' where the GOV.UK pattern for a choice is 'Select'.

claims.statement: A blank phone number is refused with 'Enter a telephone number', and one over the cap with 'Telephone number must be 20 characters or fewer'.
claims.note: The label reads 'Phone number' while the messages say 'telephone number'.

claims.statement: A blank email address is refused with 'Enter an email address', one in the wrong shape with 'Enter an email address in the correct format', and one over the cap with 'Email address must be 254 characters or fewer'.
The edit form's labels and error messages are the same as the INS address book's own.
claims.quote: // Labels and errors match the INS address book's (features/address-book/copy).

claims.statement: The edit form's buttons are 'Save changes' as the primary and 'Cancel' as a secondary beside it.
claims.quote:
save: 'Save changes',
  cancel: 'Cancel',
claims.note: The edit form offers neither Save and continue nor Save and return to overview.

claims.statement: The edit form opens pre-filled from the copy already on the notification: the name, phone and email from the party itself and the rest from its address.
claims.note: mechanism: reads the stored party answer into the edit form's values.

claims.statement: Saving an edit writes the name, phone and email on the party and the address lines, town or city, county, postcode and country code on its address.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the edit form's values into the party answer stored on the notification. The form captures no address line 3, although the picker's address cell shows one.

claims.statement: Saving an edit drops the record the address was picked from, so the picker no longer shows the edited copy as its chosen address.
claims.quote:
/** Leaves out `pickedFromId`: an edited copy no longer matches the record it
 * was picked from, so the picker should not pre-select it. */

claims.statement: An edit changes only this notification: the organisation's address book record is not changed.
claims.quote: await state.commit(request, h, { [party.id]: partyFrom(value) })
claims.note: The commit writes only the notification's own answers; the copy says so to the trader.

claims.statement: A valid save returns the trader to the page the edit was opened from, carrying the trail.
claims.quote: return h.redirect(returnHref(request, party))

claims.statement: The edit form returns to the page a 'return' marker names, but only when that marker names the consignment addresses page, the notification view or the consignment contact select page; any other marker is ignored and the party's own return page is used.
claims.quote:

    'addresses',

    CONTACT_PARTY.slug

claims.note: kit.CYA_SLUG is 'notification-view'. A marker that is not one of the three is logged once per request as 'Return marker not recognised, marker dropped'.

claims.statement: The edit form's back link goes to the same page its save returns to.
claims.quote: backLink: returnHref(request, party),

claims.statement: Cancel leaves the copy as it was and returns the trader to the page the edit was opened from, without saving anything.
claims.note: Cancel is checked before the answers are read, so nothing is validated and nothing is written.

claims.statement: A refused edit re-renders the form with the trader's own answers kept, an error summary above the heading and each field's message beside it, and answers with a 400.
Opening a party's edit form when nothing has been chosen for that party sends the trader to that party's picker instead, carrying the trail.
claims.note: The same guard runs on the POST, so a save against a party with no answer is redirected too.

claims.statement: An edit the service cannot persist re-renders the form with the trader's answers, marked as a recoverable error, and answers with a 500.
An unanswered field posts as an empty string rather than being left out, so every field is validated on every save.
claims.quote:
const valuesFrom = (payload = {}) =>
  Object.fromEntries(FIELDS.map((field) => [field, payload[field] ?? '']))
claims.note: mechanism: reads the posted form into the nine known fields and ignores anything else posted.

claims.statement: The same address rules are used to judge whether a party's stored copy is complete, so a party whose copy breaks any of them is not treated as answered.
claims.quote:
export const isValidParty = (party, countryCodes) =>
  validate(addressRules(countryCodes), formValuesOf(party)).errors === null

claims.statement: The edit form has no serious or critical accessibility violations.
The addresses feature's Welsh copy carries the same keys as its English copy, including every key the picker uses, and is marked as a machine draft that has not been reviewed by a translator.
claims.quote: // MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator. Do not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
claims.note: Read for key parity only, not string by string. Its picker keys mirror the English: caption, search label, hint and button, errorPrefix, noMatches, selectedAddress, resultsHeading, resultsCount, pagination, table, selectRowPrefix, view, addNewAddress and handshakeErrors.

claims.statement: The party edit form's Welsh copy carries the same keys as its English copy, title, hint, the nine field labels, the phone hint, the country select text, the two buttons and every error message, and is marked as a machine draft that has not been reviewed by a translator.
claims.quote: // MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator. Do not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
claims.note: Read for key parity only, not string by string.

claims.statement: The picker offers no way to clear a chosen address once one is ticked: there is no 'none of these' option and no remove control on the page.
claims.note: Looked in _address-picker.njk, _cells.njk, party-picker.njk and party-picker.controller.js. The radios cannot be unticked and the hidden 'selected' field carries the choice forward, so only the addresses page's own controls could clear it.

claims.statement: The picker offers no sort control and no choice of page size: the order is the address book's and the page size is fixed at eight.
claims.note: Looked in the picker template, its macros and the whole view-model folder.

claims.statement: The picker reads the whole list of the organisation's addresses for the role and then cuts a page out of it in the frontend, rather than asking the address book for one page.
claims.note: mechanism: the address book client reads every page of the list API at the maximum page size, four pages at a time, before the picker pages the result for display.

claims.statement: The picker's View link into the INS address book is not proven end to end by the fit suite, because the suite runs in stub mode where the link is not offered.
claims.note: Looked in both fit specs. hub-picker.fit.spec.js asserts the add-address control and the View column are absent in stub mode, so only the unit tests cover the link itself.

claims.statement: The party edit form's country select, its phone hint and every over-long message are not proven by its fit spec, which asserts only the name and County fields, the save, the postcode required message and Cancel.
claims.note: Looked at all five tests in party-edit.fit.spec.js.

claims.statement: The picker's address cell can show an address line 3, but the edit form has no address line 3 field, so a third line cannot be entered or changed on a notification.
claims.note: Looked in address-rules.js's FIELD_RULES, party-edit.njk and party-edit/copy/copy.en.js. Which address fields a notification captures is V4's to settle.

claims.statement: Neither the picker nor the edit form offers an address search of a wider address lookup: the only search on the picker is over the organisation's own address book, and the edit form is manual entry.
claims.note: Looked in both templates and both controllers.

claims.statement: No rule on the edit form depends on which party is being edited or on which country is chosen: all six edit pages apply the same nine rules, and no field is required, optional or capped differently for a United Kingdom address than for an overseas one.
claims.note: Looked in address-rules.js, party-edit.controller.js, party-edit.njk and parties.js. The only per-party difference is the caption, the return page and which answer is written; the postcode is required and capped at 12 whatever the country.
